decisions.title: FR-6 trigger conditions 3 & 4 mechanical evaluator (deterministic predicate vs designer judgment)
decisions.context: FR-6's four trigger conditions for 'feature touches the agent surface' include two (trigger 3: 'new skill that the feature's design indicates one or more existing agents will load'; trigger 4: 'new domain concept whose skill-coverage decision names an existing agent as a downstream consumer') that require interpretive reads of Blueprint / Skill-Coverage Decisions text rather than a pure file-diff check. The parent's D-5 (OI-A6) lean was a hybrid: machine-checkable advisory derived from FR-7's table-shape output plus human ratification at Design Composition. R2a inherits that lean. Codebase researcher confirmed (C-0071) that the FR-7 table is mechanically parseable — HIGH suitability for the deterministic-predicate route.
options_summary: Deterministic predicate over FR-7 Skill-Coverage Decisions table (HIGH suitability per C-0071)
Designer-judgment with reviewer second-pass (lower precision, lower authoring burden)
Hybrid: machine-checkable advisory + human ratification (parent's lean)
risks: Uneven enforcement across runs if designer-judgment route is chosen without ratification
Hybrid carries cost: two artifacts (table + ratification log) must stay coherent
decisions.framer_notes: Open with strong recommendation toward the hybrid. The deterministic-predicate component is feasible per codebase facts; the human-ratification component handles the residual interpretive risk.

decisions.title: FR-7 W/H/A trifecta — substance heuristic vs structural mandate
decisions.context: FR-7's Skill-Coverage Decisions section mandates Why/How/Anti-patterns justification for each new domain concept. The parent's D-8 surfaced the tension: T-003 verified across 6 platforms (Anthropic, LangGraph, OpenAI, MAF, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel) that W/H/A substance is well-trodden community ground, but the *mandate to write it down at design time as a single structured artifact* is novel (C-0257). The graph reading: FR-7 is the heaviest node (23 claim back-pointers); D-8's framing is the most consequential R2a decision. Parent's lean is hybrid: full mandate when proposing a new skill; principle/substance heuristic when naming an existing skill or recording 'no skill warranted'. PRD §Product Policy already codifies 'substance over form' (decision row satisfactory iff justification cell actually answers W/H/A, not merely populates cells).
options_summary: Full structural mandate (every decision row must have populated W/H/A cells regardless of resolution type)
Principle/substance heuristic only (judge rows by whether they read as actually answering W/H/A)
Hybrid: mandate when proposing a new skill; substance heuristic for existing-skill / no-skill-warranted rows (parent's lean)
risks: Ritualism / cell-stuffing — full mandate is the most likely path into the failure mode FR-7 is designed to prevent (anti-pattern verified across T-003 6-platform survey)
Skill-coverage decision codification is novel (genesis stage) — no production precedent for the exact shape
Heaviest node in graph (23 back-pointers): framing choice ripples through FR-7 ACs, dogfood deliverable validation, and downstream consumer expectations
Substance heuristic requires reviewer judgment; risks uneven enforcement
decisions.claude_code_layer_attachment: .claude/agents/synthesize-framer.md (decision generation) + .claude/agents/design-composer.md (decision arbitration) + KB-documentation-criteria/references/templates/ (new section template per OI-R2a-4)
decisions.framer_notes: Substance heuristic is the right default; the hybrid lean is correct. This is the highest-leverage R2a decision — Synthesizer should narrate the trade-off transparently.

decisions.title: Severity-vocabulary bridge content (R2a authors content; host decided in parent)
decisions.closure_pointer: Host decided by inherited ADR-0061 (severity-vocabulary bridge table). R2a authors the bridge CONTENT.
decisions.context: Parent D-10 picked the host (`KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md`) via ADR-0061. R2a inherits the host and authors the content. Two graph facts make the content non-trivial: (1) Two severity-weight sets `conflicts_with` (E-0049 iteration-delta weights vs E-0046 verdict-compute weights; claims C-0042, C-0043, C-0092, C-0094) — the bridge must preserve both, not collapse to one. (2) Three vocabularies must be mapped (auditor BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT/INFO; reviewer critical/important/recommended; PV blocking/warning/informational). The graph's non-monotonic edges between these three vocabularies are the load-bearing content the bridge must capture.
options_summary: Document both weight sets explicitly with disambiguating context (graph-supported lean)
Collapse to one canonical weight set (loses semantic information; rejected per C-0092)
Defer weight reconciliation; bridge only maps vocabulary tiers
risks: Two weight sets conflict (E-0049 vs E-0046 per C-0042, C-0043, C-0092, C-0094): collapsing would silently break iteration-delta verdict math
20 agents load KB-review-disciplines (C-0070): any incoherent bridge content propagates broadly with no separate review surface
R2b consumer (FR-4, FR-5) inherits this content — incomplete bridge blocks R2b
decisions.framer_notes: Content decision, not architecture. Graph-supported lean toward preserving both weight sets. Synthesizer should surface the two-set conflict transparently.

decisions.title: FR-9 marker-parser realization location (agent prompt vs auditing-shared/scripts vs auditing-mcp rule)
decisions.context: ADR-0063 sets the Blocks-X grammar; the parser/regex that recognizes the marker on stage-transition checkpoints is a separate realization decision (OI-R2a-3 per PRD). Codebase researcher confirmed zero existing parser (C-0073, C-0074: grep returns no matches), so this is a green-field placement. Researcher recommended `auditing-shared/scripts/parse_blocks_x_markers.py` (C-0073) on the rationale that multiple consumers (orchestrator gate, review-architecture-auditor, auditing-subagents rule) would all dispatch to it.
options_summary: Shared script at `auditing-shared/scripts/parse_blocks_x_markers.py` (researcher's recommendation; serves multiple consumers)
Inline in `review-architecture-auditor` agent prompt (LLM-side parsing; couples regex to one agent)
Inside an auditing-mcp rule (couples to MCP audit surface)
risks: Single-sourced supporting claim: C-0073 (codebase researcher's recommendation, no external corroboration)
Shared-script route requires the consuming agents to actually invoke it — predicate is grep-checkable per NFR-9 but discipline-bound
decisions.framer_notes: Two-way door; lean toward the shared script per researcher recommendation. Single-sourced but the recommendation derives from inspectable codebase facts (zero existing parser; multiple prospective consumers).

decisions.title: FR-7 artifact location (standalone `skill-coverage-decisions.md` vs embed in synthesis/design)
decisions.context: OI-R2a-4 asks whether FR-7's Skill-Coverage Decisions section is a standalone file or a section embedded in existing synthesis/blueprint/cc-design templates. Codebase researcher recommends embed (C-0069, C-0075: no precedent for standalone artifact; embed has lower irreversibility). C-0076 confirms zero existing `skill-coverage*` files. Per the inherited D-8 substance heuristic, location is secondary to substance — but it does determine whether the section is auto-surfaced in the natural authoring workflow (embed) or requires authors to discover a new file (standalone).
options_summary: Embed as section template in synthesis/blueprint/cc-design templates (researcher's recommendation; surfaces in existing workflow)
Standalone `working/feature/<slug>/skill-coverage-decisions.md` (greppable but discovery-burden on authors)
Hybrid: section embedded in synthesis (where candidates surface) + appended to design (where decisions are resolved)
risks: Embed risks dilution (section may be skimmed under template clutter)
Standalone risks discovery cost (authors must learn a new file)
Embed is two-way reversible to standalone if discovery-cost evidence is collected later
decisions.framer_notes: Embed lean per researcher. Two-way door — low-risk to start embed and reassess if substance heuristic enforcement requires a more visible artifact.

decisions.title: FR-10 audit rule realization (new rule entry vs extend existing rule)
decisions.context: OI-R2a-5 asks whether FR-10's `auditing-subagents` rule is added as a new rule entry or extends an existing rule. Codebase researcher recommends new rule (C-0066, C-0077, C-0078): zero existing rules predicate on 'feature working directory shape' (C-0066), the new script signature accepts a feature-slug parameter (C-0067) which differs from existing scripts' `.claude/agents/<file>.md` shape (C-0067), and grep for `working/feature` / `working-directory` in auditing-subagents/ returns zero (C-0078). The shape mismatch is the load-bearing reason — bolting onto an existing rule would distort its contract.
options_summary: Add new rule entry SA-NN + new script (researcher's recommendation; clean separation)
Extend an existing rule's predicate (compresses code surface but conflates audit dimensions)
Add new script under auditing-shared/ but keep rule entry in auditing-subagents (decouple shared parser from rule registry)
risks: New rule increases rule count — minor discipline-tracking cost
Extending an existing rule risks the predicate-shape mismatch (C-0067) silently breaking existing consumers
decisions.claude_code_layer_attachment: .claude/skills/auditing-subagents/ (new rule entry + new script accepting feature-slug)
decisions.framer_notes: Strong lean to new rule. Codebase facts (C-0066, C-0067, C-0078) all point one way.

decisions.title: Plan-stage sequencing (severity-bridge content first vs FR-1/9/10 sections that consume it)
decisions.context: OI-R2a-6 (PRD) asks how to sequence severity-taxonomy bridge content authoring vs FR-1/9/10 sections that consume it. Codebase researcher confirmed (C-0079, C-0080) bridge content is purely additive — no collision with existing content (`git diff --stat` on `severity-taxonomy.md` returns empty). The natural sequence: author bridge content first (so consumers reference real content, not placeholder), then author FR-1/9/10 sections that cite the bridge. This is a low-blast-radius sequencing call, not an architectural choice.
options_summary: Bridge content first, then FR-1/9/10 sections (researcher's lean)
FR sections first with bridge placeholders, then back-fill bridge
Parallel (single Plan-stage tracker handles both)
risks: If FR sections are authored first with placeholders, plan must enforce the back-fill — discipline risk only
